newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CERA TO AWARD ITS FIRST CREDIT RATING SOON.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CERA TO AWARD ITS FIRST CREDIT RATING SOON.

text.p: Poland's Central European Rating Agency (CERA) will soon award its first rating after signing an agreement with chemical firm EMA-Blachownia SA, which plans a 1.2 million-zloty convertible bond issue, CERA head said.
"It is the first step towards creating a credit risk framework for the Polish debt market," Wojciech Lipka said in a statement on Thursday.
Lipka also said the agreement showed that credit rating could be useful not only for public debt issues but also for private placements such as Blachownia's.
CERA SA, established in 1996, is the first Polish rating agency. Its ratings will be published in its bulletin "Rating & Rynek."
